# Backups

The studio's records live on a single laptop and a small network drive: orders, invoices, glaze recipes and photographs of every collection. Losing the glaze recipes alone would set us back years of testing.

## What gets backed up

The network drive copies the laptop's documents folder every night at midnight. Photographs are backed up weekly because the files are large and rarely change once edited. Once a month, Elena copies everything to an encrypted external drive which she keeps at home. Nightly copies are kept for one month, monthly copies for a full year.

## Restoring files

We restore one random folder every quarter to check that the backups actually work. The last test recovered the glaze recipe folder in about ten minutes, and every file opened correctly. If a restore ever fails, we contact the IT contractor the same day and stop deleting old copies until the problem is understood.

## Passwords

The external drive and the online account share nothing: each has its own long password stored in a sealed envelope in the office safe. Passwords are changed whenever someone with access leaves the studio.
